solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He'd argue if forced out for one fronting the organisation

indicators.note: the letters of these words are forced out of their order into a new one

explanation.surface: Someone says a man would protest if he were pushed out of his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced out' rearranges HEDARGUEIF; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead is the nominal leader at the front of a body, with little real power.

clue.text: Works hard for heartless families hoarding silver

indicators.note: the ends of families keep the silver stored between them
the inner letters of families are removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Grafting away for impoverished households that are stashing away silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves F and S from families; 'hoarding' puts AG between them. To fag is British slang for toil.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage to fag means to labour wearily, so it fits the verb phrase about toiling.

clue.text: Bird droppings covering a cold creature from the Andes

indicators.note: the droppings are wrapped around the other pieces like a coat

parts.note: guano is the accumulated excrement of seabirds
C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Bird mess lands on a chilly animal living in South American mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The guanaco is a wild camelid, relative of the llama, native to the Andes.

clue.text: The reality of an obscene call in the morning?

parts.note: rude can mean vulgar or offensive
being roused from sleep at dawn is a wake-up call

explanation.surface: A dirty phone call at breakfast time brings you down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lewd early phone call; read literally it is a crude rousing, and the phrase means a sudden unwelcome confrontation with the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude awakening is a shock of discovering how things really are, a harsh dose of reality.

clue.text: Saving a place for notices

definitions.meaning: putting money or goods aside, as a store kept up
a large board on which posters and advertisements are displayed

explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding means amassing a store, and in Britain also a billboard for posters.

clue.text: Romeo is in endless pain, due to gas

indicators.note: the letter for Romeo sits inside the shortened word for pain
the last letter of the word for pain is cut off

parts.note: agony is extreme suffering
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lovesick young man is suffering terribly because of some vapour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts AGONY to AGON; 'is in' puts R inside; 'due to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas found in the air.

clue.text: Feature of street in stockbroker belt

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Something you might see on a road in a wealthy commuter suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: The stockbroker belt is the affluent commuter area around London; the answer runs across stockbroKER Belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerb is the raised edge of a pavement beside the road, the British spelling of curb.

clue.text: I heard and fired in range

indicators.note: the pronoun I is said aloud, giving the word for the organ of sight

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
a shot is something discharged from a gun

explanation.surface: Someone hears and fires at a target within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshot is the distance one can see, the range of vision.

clue.text: They may be laid on for midnight feasts

definitions.text: They may be laid on for midnight feasts

parts.words: They may be laid on for midnight feasts
parts.note: read as food laid out, it suggests snacks; really it is coverings on a bed, the place of such feasts

explanation.surface: Things provided for children's late-night secret parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid on' suggests catering, but a midnight feast is eaten in bed, and these coverings lie on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedspreads are decorative covers laid over beds, where dormitory midnight feasts take place.

clue.text: Member of family of the majority of top chess players

indicators.note: most of the word is kept and its last few letters are cut away

parts.note: grandmasters hold the highest title in chess

explanation.surface: A relative of most of the world's best chess players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority of' keeps seven of twelve letters, dropping STERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is a family member, and the short form is an everyday word for her.

clue.text: Despatch by returning setter, say, is a stroke of good fortune

indicators.note: the word for the dog is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, signalled by say as an example
to despatch something is to send it

explanation.surface: Sending a message via a crossword compiler who comes back proves lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the crossword compiler, but it is the gun dog. 'returning' turns DOG into GOD; 'by' places it beside SEND; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected welcome boon, a piece of luck.

clue.text: Mother's partner yearns to grab stage and fly

parts.note: the father, alongside mummy, is daddy

indicators.note: the word for yearns takes hold of the stage inside it

parts.note: longs means desires strongly
a leg is one stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Dad pines to seize the theatre stage and then escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like a verb to flee but is the insect; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A daddy-longlegs is the British name for the crane fly, a long-legged insect.

clue.text: Dissolute son with joint left failing organisation

parts.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained in morals
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A wayward son with a reefer quit a collapsing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette but is the body's hip; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon ship is to quit a doomed enterprise, figuratively a venture that is failing.

clue.text: Exposed cards used without us being generous

parts.note: open means uncovered or laid bare
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

indicators.note: the letters of us are taken out of used

explanation.surface: Showing your cards when the game is played without us is a kindly gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes US from USED, leaving ED; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed gives freely, liberal with money and gifts.

clue.text: Compound transforming some paint without sulphur

indicators.note: the remaining letters are changed into a new order
the letter for sulphur is taken out of these words

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Some chemical compound is changing a bit of paint once the sulphur is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes S from SOMEPAINT to leave OMEPAINT, which 'transforming' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaine is a chemical substance formed when protein putrefies, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Go through wood on the way back, finding shrub

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read in reverse, as if travelling back
the attempt goes inside the tree

parts.note: elm is a tree and its timber
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Walking through a forest on the return path, someone comes across a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like the verb but is a noun, an attempt; the reversed result is ELTRYM read backwards, and 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Make complicated but disastrous net approach

indicators.note: the word net is wrecked into a new arrangement

parts.note: an angle is a way of tackling a problem

explanation.surface: A fishing net is a terrible way to go about things, making matters messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' turns NET into ENT; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to twist up or involve in difficulties, making something intricate.

clue.text: Whipped, getting cut

definitions.meaning: suffering a small nick or scratch

explanation.definitionFit: Nicked is British slang for stolen, and also describes skin given a small cut.

clue.text: Fortune left for section of church

parts.note: chance means luck or fortune

explanation.surface: Luck was abandoned in a part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar where clergy and choir sit.

clue.text: Noted eccentric being given honour and buried

indicators.note: the honour is placed within the rearranged letters
the word noted is treated oddly and rearranged

parts.note: an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A famous oddball receives an award and is later laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' gives ENTOD from the first word; 'Noted' looks like an adjective for a famous person but is the fodder, and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Entombed means placed in a tomb, laid to rest.

clue.text: Person supplying drink advocates one's expression of gratitude

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers collectively
one is I, and the possessive adds S
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A drinks server thanks the lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes and serves coffee in a café.

clue.text: Off home during the morning, heading off risk from a seasonal song

parts.note: away means absent, gone off
in means at home
a.m. denotes the morning

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for risk is removed

parts.note: danger means hazard or risk

explanation.surface: Leaving the house early, someone avoids hazards from a Christmas carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the D of DANGER; 'during' and 'from a' link the pieces. The answer is a Christmas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Christmas carol about the nativity, sung each December.

clue.text: PA system with no time to bug

indicators.note: the letter for time is dropped from the brand name

parts.note: Tannoy is a British brand name used generally for public address systems

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker setup, lacking time, used to irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or pester them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Tool for cutting commercials on the radio

indicators.note: broadcast speech means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: ads are advertisements

explanation.surface: Adverts broadcast on air for a cutting implement.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like tool with an arched blade for shaping wood.

clue.text: The shape of accountant shot in study

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private room for work
CA is a chartered accountant
a go is a try or shot

explanation.surface: An accountant was killed in his office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a shooting but means an attempt. 'The' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane figure with ten sides.

clue.text: King grew less severe, becoming lubricated

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
eased means became milder

explanation.surface: The monarch softened, becoming well-oiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Greased means smeared with oil or fat to reduce friction.

clue.text: State assistance finally provided cheer in Spain

indicators.note: only the last letter of provided is used

parts.note: olé is the Spanish shout of approval

explanation.surface: Government help eventually gave Spanish people something to cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit paid by government.

clue.text: Scrap EEC by developing international links

indicators.note: the letters evolve into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ditch the European Community by building global ties.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the online realm of computer networks connecting the world.
